rule:
Maisons Sur-Mer in Horry County's public records, in aggregate.
1. Parcels: https://www.horrycounty.org/parcelapp/rest/services/HorryCountyGISApp/MapServer/24/query, every parcel whose
   LegalDescr starts "THE PALACE;" (the regime name /invest/condo-buildings/ used). Units = parcels with a building value.
   Kept: units per floor (floor = the unit number less its last two digits), door numbers per floor, the count of units at
   each county market value (the assessor's unit types), the year of each unit's last recorded sale (counts), owner mailing
   state (counts), units taxed at the 4% legal-residence ratio. Never kept: a PIN, an owner, a unit's own record.
2. Sales: the deed sales /invest/condo-buildings/ used (data/2026-10-d/sell-out-of-state-buyers/out-of-state-buyers.json,
   AcclaimWeb DEED (001) recorded 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30, kept sales only), plus the later window 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31
   (data/2026-11-n/buyers-builders/raw/deeds-co.json, Consideration > 0). Kept: count, median, quartiles, range, by floor band,
   and buyers' tax-bill state (in or out of South Carolina) for the first window.
Run: python3 -I pull_county.py <this dir> <website root>. Writes county.json.

floors.note: floor = the number after FL (or F) in the legal description

later_window.note: Joined to this regime's parcels by parcel number. Deeds under $1,000 are transfers, not sales

sales_by_value.rule:
Maisons Sur-Mer: recorded sales split by the county's own market value for the unit (a stand-in for the plan, since deeds carry no
bedrooms): units valued under $400,000 (23 units, one door line of 11), $400,000 to $699,999 (the great majority) and $700,000 or more
(the top floors and a few others). Sources: Horry County GIS layer 24 (PIN, MarketProp, LegalDescr '%MAISON%SUR%MER%'), joined by PIN to the deed
files named in pull_county.py (window 1: out-of-state-buyers.json, 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30; window 2: data/2026-11-n/buyers-builders/raw/deeds-co.json,
2025-11-01 to 2026-10-31, Consideration >= 1000). Kept: per group the count, median, lowest and highest price (a group under 3 is not kept).
Never kept: a PIN, a unit, a buyer, a date of a single deed. Run: python3 -I pull_sales_by_value.py <this dir> <website root>. Merges "sales_by_value" into county.json.
